sentences.text:
Raj Kumar and another ....Appellants
 V/s
Madhu Sudan Kumar and others ....Respondents
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Vikram Aggarwal
Present: Ms. Saksham Sharma, Advocate, for the appellants.

Mr. D.P. Gupta, Advocate for respondent No.3-insurance co.
 Mr. Mohit Kaushik, Advocate for
 Mr. Vishwajit Bedi, Advocate, for respondent No.5.

* * *
Vikram Aggarwal, J. (Oral)

The present appeal has been filed against the award dated 01.06.2010 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhiwani (hereinafter referred to as "the MACT"), whereby the claim petition filed by the appellants under Sections 163-A/166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short "the MV Act"), seeking compensation on account of death of Harikesh alias Hari Kishan, was dismissed.

2. The facts as emanating from the paperbook are that on 27.12.2006, at about 5:00 A.M.,
deceased-Harikesh alias Hari Kishan was driving truck bearing Regn. No.HR-46-B-6548 (hereinafter referred to as "the non-offending vehicle") towards Samtel Factory situated at Bulandsahar Road. When the said truck reached near Hapur Chowk, another truck bearing Regn.
No.HR-38-M-9269 (hereinafter referred to as "the offending vehicle") allegedly driven by respondent No.1 in a rash and negligent manner and at a high speed, came from the opposite direction and collided with the non-offending vehicle.

As a result of the said collision, 1 of 6 FAO-262-2011 (O&M) -2- Harikesh @ alias Hari Kishan (hereinafter referred to as "the deceased")
sustained multiple grievous injuries and died at the spot.
The body of the deceased was taken to the Government Hospital, Gaziabad, where its post- mortem was conducted.

FIR No.573 dated 27.12.2006 under Sections 279, 337, 304A IPC was registered at Police Station Gaziabad on the statement of Mani Shankar Upadhyay, who was stated to be an employee of respondent No.4.
3.

It was averred in the claim petition that the deceased was unmarried and working as a professional driver earning about Rs.5,000/- per month and the appellants being his elder brothers,
were totally dependent upon his income.

sentences.text: Upon notice, respondents No.1 and 2 i.e., the driver and owner of the offending vehicle, appeared and filed their written statement admitting the factum of the accident but denied the allegations and pleaded that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the deceased himself.
It was further pleaded that a false FIR had been lodged against respondent No.1.

5. Respondent No.3 i.e. Insurance Company of the offending vehicle also filed its written statement raising similar pleas and contended that respondent No.1 was not holding a valid and effective driving licence at the time of the accident.

6. Respondent No.4 i.e. the owner of the non-offending vehicle supported the case of the appellant-claimants and alleged that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
7. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the following issues were framed:-

"1. Whether the accident which occurred on 27.12.2006 causing 2 of 6 FAO-262-2011 (O&M) -3- death of Harikesh @ Hari Kishan son of Shri Rampal Singh due to rash and negligent driving of respondent No.1 while driving the Dumpher No.HR-38-M-9269?
OPP 2.
If issue No.1 is proved, whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation, if so to what amount and from whom?OPP 3.

Whether the driver of the offending vehicle i.e. respondent No.1 was not holding the valid driving license on the date of accident and the vehicle in question was being driven in violation of the terms and conditions of the issuance policy at the time of accident?OPR 4.
Whether the respondent No.3 is liable to indemnify the compensation to the claimant?OPR 5.
Whether the present petition is not maintainable in its present form?OPR 6. Relief."
8. Parties led their respective evidence.

9. As regards the issue of negligence, the MACT came to the conclusion that the appellants had failed to prove that the accident had taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver and dismissed the claim petition.
10. Aggrieved by the aforesaid decision, the claimants-appellants have instituted the present appeal.
11. I have heard learned counsel for the parties.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the MACT erred in dismissing the claim petition as the proceedings under the MV Act are to be decided on the principle of preponderance of probabilities and strict proof as required in criminal cases is not necessary.

It is further argued that keeping in view the facts and circumstances on record, it was apparent that as a matter of fact, the accident had taken place on account of the negligence of respondent no. 1, as pleaded by the claimants and, thus, the claim petition filed by the claimants ought to have been allowed by the MACT by applying the doctrine of res ipsa loquitur.
3 of 6

. On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the respondent-Insurance Company, while defending the impugned award, submits that in the absence of any eye witness account and in view of the testimonies of the witnesses examined by the appellant-claimants, no illegality can be found in the finding recorded by the MACT that the appellant-claimants had failed to establish negligence on the part of respondent No.1.
14. I have considered the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties.

15. The issue which arises for consideration is as to whether the claimants were able to establish that the accident in question occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent No.1.
It is well settled that proceedings before the MACT are to be decided on the basis of preponderance of probabilities and strict proof of negligence as required in criminal trials is not necessary.
However, the claimants are still required to place on record some material establishing negligence on the part of the offending vehicle.
In the present case, the claimants examined PW1 (Mani Shankar Upadhyay), on the basis of whose statement, the FIR was registered.
However, in his cross-examination, he denied having witnessed the accident and further stated that the FIR produced on record did not bear his signatures.
He further stated that he could not state as to what had been written in the FIR.
16. Similarly, PW2 (Balwan Singh), who is one of the claimants, admitted that he was not present at the spot at the time of the accident and that he had not witnessed the occurrence.
17. Thus, neither of the witnesses examined by the claimants, was an eye witness to the accident.
No independent witness had been produced 4 of 6 FAO-262-2011 (O&M) -5- to establish the manner in which the accident occurred.

The FIR alone cannot be treated as a substantive piece of evidence to prove the negligence, particularly when the person, who allegedly lodged the FIR, had denied witnessing the accident and had even disputed his signatures on the said document.
No final report was brought on record.
Further, the appellants have invoked the principle of res ipsa loquitur.

However, the said doctrine applies only in cases where the nature of the accident itself clearly (O&M) Raj Kumar And Anr vs Madhu Sudan Kumar And Ors on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43131686/
3 indicates negligence of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: In the present case, the accident involved collision between two trucks coming from the opposite directions and in the absence of any evidence regarding the manner of driving of either vehicle, it cannot be presumed that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the offending vehicle alone.
Even applying the principle of preponderance of probabilities, the claimants have failed to place any material on record from which negligence of respondent No.1 could reasonably be inferred.

The finding recorded by the learned MACT that the appellants had failed to establish that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of respondent No.1 is based on proper appreciation of the evidence and does not suffer from any illegality.

18. I have gone through the judgments relied upon by learned counsel for the appellants in the cases of Bimla Devi and ors. versus Himachal Road Transport Corpn. and ors. 2009 (13) SCC 530, Kusum Lata and others versus Satbir and others 2011 (3) SCC 646 and ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company versus Smt. Moni and ors. 2024 (4) Law Herald 3289.

sentences.text: There is absolutely no dispute in the ratio laid down in the said judgments.
However, they would not come to the aid of the appellants, in view of the peculiar facts of the present case.
5 of 6
That being so, finding no merit in the appeal, the same is dismissed.
Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of.

(VIKRAM AGGARWAL)
 JUDGE March 06, 2026 vcgarg
